relation: coefficient of Q^+_(y_k) = delta y_k + (y_k/2)(delta Z_f1 + delta Z_f2 + delta Z_H), delta Z_f = -(C_f + calY_f)/(16 pi^2 eps) (coefficient of Q^f_K, g0_FF), delta Z_H = -(Y_2 - 2 C_H)/(16 pi^2 eps) (coefficient of the d-dimensional Q_SS, g0_SS; the evanescent E_H, Etilde_H poles of g0_SS do not enter), Y_2 = 3y_u^2+3y_d^2+y_e^2

Two independent calculations (deriver: hand; checker: toolkit) and the referee's own explicit-matrix script agree per topology, per vertex and per SU(2) component of the external scalar
delta Z_f agrees with g0_FF final_result.json (coefficient of Q^f_K); delta Z_H agrees with the g0_SS deriver and checker results (coefficient of Q_SS = -(Y_2 - 2 C_H)/(16 pi^2 eps))

Literature: gauge part C_H + 4 t_k = BIMS (2004.14398) eq. (5.14) at xi=1 (xi C_2(S) + (3+xi) T_Rbar Y T_R / Y); fermion self-energy = BIMS eq. (5.10); full pole parts equal targets_in_our_conventions.md sec. 3; beta functions are the standard one-generation SM ones
caveats: Feynman gauge only; the split of the gauge part between nu_k and delta Z is gauge dependent, delta y_k is not (consistency with the standard beta functions checked; general xi not computed here, but BIMS (5.14) gives xi C_H + (3+xi) t_k for the vertex)
